meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

подумать.gloss: to think (for a while), to think it over

meanings.en: to think (for a while), to think it over
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (for a while), to think it over', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

перейти.gloss: to cross, switch, move on to

meanings.en: to cross, switch, move on to
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cross, switch, move on to', paired with 'переходить'.

examples.text: А теперь перейдём к другим новостям.
examples.trans: And now let us move on to other news.

examples.text: А теперь перешли к другим новостям.
examples.trans: And now they moved on to other news.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to feel', paired with 'почувствовать'.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fault, guilt, blame' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I will make up for my fault.
Forgive me, I will make up for my fault.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to figure out
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'обраться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Borrowed via Polish/German from Greek 'problema' (something thrown forward, a task or question).

examples.trans: I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth; honestly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'because of; from behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Из-за вашей Лёли весь класс зовёт меня врунишкой!
examples.trans: Because of your Lyolya the whole class calls me a little liar!
We were late because of the rain.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.en: for a long time; long ago
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offer, to suggest', paired with 'предлагать'.

examples.trans: But you were offered a job.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу. Что, плохая работа?
examples.trans: But you were offered a job. What, is it a bad job?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'веренный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('confident, sure').

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный.
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident.
He answered in a calm, confident voice.

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный. Что конкретно?
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident. What specifically?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'for nothing, in vain', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время. Шпионить для вас я не буду.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'потерять'.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время. Шпионить для вас я не буду.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'right, really (colloq.)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ращать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to turn, to direct', paired with 'обратить'.
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'attention' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А ну-ка, дай посмотрю! Внимание, ребята!
examples.trans: Hold on, let me have a look! Attention, everyone!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
See the markers? They're from Japan!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'eye' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!
